text:
How the Cladding Safety Scheme (CSS) works and how to apply

Apply for funding

Funding applications are made online using the Building Remediation Hub website.

You will need to sign into your existing account if you have one or register for an account.

What you’ll need

You will need to provide:

building details

details of the responsible entity and their contact information

evidence you are authorised to make an application on behalf of a responsible entity

evidence of leaseholder engagement (to ensure they are aware of your application for funding)

details of any alternative sources of funding you have explored or are in progress

bank account details for the account you would want funding paid into if successful

If you start a funding application other people in your organisation are now able to contribute to, and submit, an application that you had started.

If you have an individual account and do not belong to an organisation

To collaborate on applications with colleagues, you can:

create an organisation

be invited to join an organisation that has already been created

As a member of an organisation, you can contribute to, and submit, any application created by someone who is part of the organisation.

If you join an organisation, any applications you create, and any later applications, are owned by the organisation. This change is permanent — even if you are later removed from the organisation.

Help with your application from people inside your organisation

You can share applications with other people in your organisation to get their help completing them.

If a person is not already part of your organisation you can invite them to join as member. You do this from the ‘Organisation Management’ tile on the dashboard. If your invitation is accepted they will be asked to set up an account if they do not already have one.

People can only be part of one organisation.

Creating an organisation

You can create an organisation from the ‘Organisation Management’ tile on the dashboard.

To do this you will need your:

company name

registration number — find your company information

If you create an organisation you automatically take on the role of administrator (admin) for that organisation.

You will always have the role of admin unless you are removed from the organisation.

Managing an organisation

Each organisation must have a minimum of 1 admin and a maximum of 2 admins. An organisation can have an unlimited number of members.

Admins can:

view, create and update applications

view a list of members

invite new members

remove members

edit details of members

Members can:

view, create and update applications assigned to the organisation

view a list of members

Inviting people to your organisation as an admin

As an admin you can invite people to become a member of the organisation.

You can do this from the ‘Organisation Management’ tile on the dashboard using the ‘Invite Member’ link.

For each member you want to invite you must provide:

their name

their e-mail address — they must share an email address domain (the part of an email address that follows the @ symbol) with you

the role you want them to take on (admin or member)

You must confirm that you understand the risks and responsibilities to allow your invite to be sent.

The invitee will appear in the list of organisation members where their status will change to:

remove — if they accepted

re-invite — if they declined

Being invited to an organisation

If you have been invited to an organisation you will receive an email.

This will include the name of the person which has sent you the invitation and allows you to accept or decline the invite.

If you accept, you’ll be asked to sign into your account or register one if you do not have one already.

Members of an organisation can see:

all applications in the organisation

any applications they have created before joining the organisation, now owned by the organisation they have joined

Editing, removing, or re-inviting people

Admins can change member details from the ‘Organisation Management’ tile on the dashboard. Select ‘Edit’ next to the name of the member you want to amend.

Admins can also remove other users in the organisation from the member list. Select ‘Remove’ next to the name of the member you want to remove.

When a person is removed their account is deactivated. They still appear in the member list and can be re-invited to the organisation by an admin. If they accept an invitation, their account will be reactivated.

Help with your application from people outside your organisation (third-party contributors)

You can invite people from outside your organisation to help you with your application.

As part of your application you’ll be asked, in the ‘Progress Reporting’ stage, to provide details of your project team. You can then choose to invite members of the project team to collaborate with you on that application as third-party contributors.

Third-party users will only be able to view, edit or add to the application to which they are invited. They can also invite and remove members of the project team.

To invite a third-party contributor, select ‘View third-party contributors’ from the home screen and select the ‘Invite’ link next to the name of the person you want to invite.

Your invitee will receive an invite by email which they can accept or decline.

The invitee will appear in the list of organisation members as invited. Their status will change to:

remove — if they accepted

re-invite — if they declined

If they accept, they will be asked to sign in to their account or register for one. This will allow them to view the select application they have been invited to from the ‘View existing applications’ list.

Admins can also remove third-party contributors from the contributors list by selecting ‘Remove access’.

When a third-party contributor is removed their edits and additions will be retained.

If you remove or replace a person from your project team during the project, you will also need to remove their access to the application.

Managing multi-year programmes

If your remediation programmes span multiple years you can add forecast dates to your applications and building records for:

start on site

practical completion

investigation completion (obtaining a Fire Risk Assessment (FRA) or Fire Risk Appraisal of External Walls (FRAEW))

Dates can be added from the ‘Manage Profile’ tile on the Building Remediation Hub dashboard.

All applications are ‘active’ by default until programme dates are added. Applications can be viewed in the ‘Manage Active Applications’ tile.

Buildings which have an investigation completion and, or, a start on site date in future years will become ‘inactive’.

Inactive buildings will not be shown in the ‘Manage Active Applications’ tile. You will not be able to access them until they become ‘active’. This happens when 1 or more of the following occurs:

a date moves out of the inactive timeframe

a user edits the date

All users can add programme dates but do not have to do so.

Resident and leaseholder engagement

You must provide evidence throughout your application and project that residents leaseholders have been kept informed and that they are aware of the following:

you have applied to the CSS

you have completed a FRAEW, which includes a clear outcome, outlines building safety issues and proposes a solution with next steps

information on the procurement of contractors and options being submitted for approval

You must provide evidence of resident and leaseholder engagement throughout the lifetime of the works programme. This is a condition of your grant payment as set out in the Code of Practice for the remediation of residential buildings. Homes England has set out the minimum requirements and this will be issued to providers.

Information required on the bank account to be used for receipt of grant funding

Whilst the grant funding agreement (GFA) will always be made with the Responsible Entity, we’ll pay the grant to the organisation that lets the contract to fix the building and pays the contractor and other professionals. So, you need to first decide who will perform this role - the Responsible Entity or their representative.

If you’re a Responsible Entity based outside the UK, you must use a representative in the UK to administer the funding and provide their bank account details.

Paying a representative

If you decide that the representative will perform this role, provide details of the bank account they’ll use to pay the contractor and receive the grant funding. In the case of representatives, we’ll only pay the funds into a bank account protected by the Client Money Protection Scheme or an equivalent. We’ll ask you to provide evidence that your (or your representative’s) organisation is registered under a Client Money Protection Scheme (CMPS). This regime includes CM Protect, UKALA, RICS, NALS, ARLA Propertymark and Money Shield. Where a representative is unable to evidence their registration via a suitable CMPS they will be required to enter into a deed of trust with Homes England.

Accrual of interest

If you earn interest on CSS funding you have received, you can use this to pay for CSS costs. You must account for this interest as part of the first claim you make after starting on site. Further funding is paid monthly in arrears so it is unlikely further interest will be earned. We review this when your final claim is made and take it into consideration when making the final 5% retention payment.

Paying a Responsible Entity

If the Responsible Entity is paying the contractor and receiving the grant, they should provide their own bank account details. We’ll also ask that the Responsible Entity enters into a legal agreement called a deed of trust, which is sent with the grant funding agreement. The deed of trust is to reassure us that the funds will be used to pay for agreed works to fix the cladding, including design and project management. The money we pay into your nominated bank account cannot be used for any other purpose. This is to ensure that this public funding is used appropriately.

A link to the deed of trust is provided so you can see the terms. This is for information only - we will send the actual document to be signed at the appropriate point in the process.

When applying and providing the bank account details, please ensure that you have considered the guidance above. If you intend to change the bank details at any point during the project, you must advise us immediately, and prior to the change if possible. It is possible to change bank account details but this takes time and could mean a delay to grant funding being paid.

All bank account information provided to us, is subject to an independent verification process which includes digital and telephone checks. This is to ensure that public funds are administered safely. We expect bank account owners to engage with this process in a timely manner.

The Fire Risk Appraisal of External Walls (FRAEW)

To apply to the CSS, you will need a Fire Risk Appraisal of External Walls (FRAEW) that follows and meets the PAS 9980:2022[footnote 5] methodology.

Homes England has set up a panel of firms which can carry out FRAEWs, who are familiar with the CSS and the scheme’s reporting requirements. Once you have submitted the information for the initial application, the FRAEW assessor panel, contact details and regions covered are visible within the system.

Please use only firms on our assessor panel to undertake a FRAEW for buildings applying to the CSS.

You’ll need to contact one of the firms on the panel to arrange and pay for the FRAEW. It’s up to you who you choose to appoint from the assessor panel. You will receive their completed report along with a standard FRAEW summary. You will need to upload both the report and the summary and, input the information from the summary into the system before submitting your application.

All FRAEW evidence is reviewed and we may engage directly with the firm who undertook your FRAEW to clarify any queries alongside undertaking required assurance to ensure a consistent approach across the scheme.

All FRAEW commercial and contractual arrangements are to be managed between the applicant and the panel member. Homes England does not take responsibility for relationship management between parties.

If the building is determined as eligible for the fund, reasonable costs associated with the FRAEW will be reimbursed as part of the grant funding at a later stage. We will not make any financial payments for buildings which are not eligible or do not need remediation.

Pre-tender support is available (and may be mandatory) for eligible social sector applicants and can be used to help with the costs of a FRAEW. From 1 November 2023 all FRAEWs submitted to the Cladding Safety Scheme must have been completed by a firm on the assessor panel.

Once you receive your FRAEW and summary and have input it into the digital system, you can submit your application. It is only after you complete the declaration and submission that your application is moved to the next stage.

Fire Risk Assessment

You will need to submit the latest Fire Risk Assessment for the building as part of your Cladding Safety Scheme application.

This helps Homes England:

report comprehensively to the Ministry for Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG) on the wider unfunded scope of remediation needed across CSS buildings

understand any internal defects alongside the external cladding work Homes England funds

track the overall safety improvements being made to buildings in the scheme

Each building should already have an up-to-date Fire Risk Assessment. It’s recommended that you have this to hand during your application submission.

When uploading, you’ll be asked to enter:

the date the Fire Risk Assessment was carried out

the overall risk rating of your Fire Risk Assessment

any internal defects identified

any funding already secured to resolve these defects

You should provide Homes England with these details as soon as possible.

Eligibility Review

On submission of your application we will complete legal and project-related due diligence on the information you have provided. By submitting your application, you’re agreeing that these checks can be done and the information has been shared in line with the privacy notice.

These checks will include but are not limited to:

KYC (know your customer) checks on the responsible entity and representative (if applicable)

checks on the ownership structure and eligibility of the building

checks on the directors of the responsible entity and signatories supplied in your application

review of the FRAEW report and summary information alongside any additional assurance we have sought

Once we’ve reviewed your completed application we’ll confirm whether our checks and outcome of the FRAEW have resulted in an eligible decision. If you are not eligible or we have concerns over the assessment, we’ll write to you to explain the reasons for rejection or seek further clarification.

Pre-tender support

If your application is confirmed as eligible, we may offer pre-tender financial support. This is to assist you in taking the next steps in your project, including:

appointing a professional team

designing the works

carrying out a competitive tender to undertake the work

Pre-tender support is an advance of the full grant funding award under CSS. It forms part of the total grant awarded — it is not a separate award. Any costs covered by your pre-tender support payment must be included in your costs schedule when you submit your Works Package later in the process.

Pre-tender support is calculated as 15% of the estimated cost of your works as set out in your FRAEW report and is subject to a cap.

We will let you know the amount of pre-tender support you will be paid once your application to the Cladding Safety Scheme is confirmed as eligible.

If at any stage your CSS application turns out to be ineligible, we will recoup the value of this initial pre-tender funding from you. In addition, Homes England reserves the right to recover this funding under certain circumstances. For example, if you:

do not progress with designing your works package

do not begin obtaining quotes and tenders

do not use the funding for the purpose intended or agreed

You provided us with proposed signatories as part of your initial application. Within your eligibility letter, we will ask that you notify us if those details have changed before we send you the grant funding agreement to sign.

If you’re not sure who the correct signatories are, please check with your legal advisor before completing this section, after noting the information below within the grant funding agreement section of this guidance.

The grant funding agreement

The grant funding agreement (GFA) [footnote 6] is the legal contract between Homes England and the Responsible Entity.

The grant funding agreement has been built based on previous industry dialogue. It has been tested with users and is a non-negotiable document. If applicants would like to receive publicly funded grant monies to assist with their building remediation, they must agree and adhere to the terms of the agreement.

In cases where a representative is appointed to lead the application, and in some cases manage the funding, the GFA must still be signed by the Responsible Entity. Applicants should be aware that the commitments given in the GFA will apply to the Responsible Entity exclusively and if it chooses to appoint a representative to act on their behalf, they should be confident that the representative is aware of and will meet Homes England’s requirements as expressed in this guidance and (separately) in the GFA.

The signatories for the grant funding agreement should be the directors or other individuals authorised to sign legal agreements for your organisation. This would be the same for the deed of trust, if needed.

The GFA must be signed by all parties prior to any funding being paid. On signing the GFA, pre-tender support (where applicable) will be paid. Following the subsequent approval of a works package, a works package deed will also need to be signed by all parties and will supplement the GFA in terms of funding and timescales that have been agreed for the project.

We have made a copy of the GFA available so you can see the terms. The template is for information only — we will send you the actual copy we want you to sign if your building is eligible. This is a non-negotiable standard form document. If you want your legal advisors to review this, we suggest that you arrange this when you apply to the Cladding Safety Scheme as this will speed up your application later.

After the building has been made eligible, the GFA is signed.

The Responsible Entity (RE) remains in place throughout the remediation process and must comply with the contractual terms. In the unlikely event that the Responsible Entity enters financial difficulties and, or, a Right to Manage (RTM) organisation is formed, Homes England must be notified straight away. This ensures we can review the RE change and work out how best to handle this. You must email support@claddingsafetyscheme.co.uk with supporting evidence such as the RTM Claim Notice.

Progress reporting (pre-works package)

After all parties have signed the Grant Funding Arrangement, you must complete ‘Progress Reporting’ on the Building Remediation Hub website.

Progress reports are created on the first working day of each month. You must complete and submit a report each month to update us on the progress of your project.

If you do not complete the submit task at the end of the report information will be lost when the report for the following month is created.

The report must be completed within 5 working days. Working days are Monday to Friday, not including UK public holidays.

What you need to tell us

When completing a progress report you will be asked for information about:

Significant dates for your project

Tell us when you expect to:

submit your works package

issue a tender

apply for planning permission and building control approval

You will be able to add actual dates when known.

Your approach to the works and remaining pre-tender support

If you need to request more pre-tender funding to reach your start on site milestone you can apply for an uplift as part of your progress report submission.

Project team details

Tell us about your project team including the:

project manager

quantity surveyor

fire engineer

lead designer

lead contractor

You can also tell us about:

the grant certifying officer

the application lead

the person responsible for communication to residents (if not the applicant)

the person responsible for regulatory compliance

You should include names and company details where appropriate.

If you’re unsure about how to begin to appoint your professional team, we suggest you initially appoint a project manager, a cost consultant, or a quantity surveyor with experience in this type of construction work. They should be able to guide you through the process.

Once your grant certifying officer has been assigned, the duty of care deed will be issued. At this stage, you will not be able to change company details for the grant certifying officer without contacting Homes England.

Resident and leaseholder communications

You should provide evidence of your resident and leaseholder communications to date.

Additional support

You can tell us if you need any support as part of your progress report each month. We will contact you to discuss how we can help progress your building remediation works.

Future progress reports

The submission of a progress report every month is required as stated in your contract. We monitor submissions to make sure they are submitted in time and are of good quality.

Once you have submitted your first monthly progress report, you will find that reports for the months that follow pre-populate some information. Before submitting progress reports check that any pre-populated information remains current. Remove any incorrect information and provide the correct details.

Decanting residents

If you need to decant a building for remediation works you should let us know by emailing support@claddingsafetyscheme.co.uk. Quote the application reference and building name.

Let us know that you intend to decant residents as soon as possible and definitely ahead of the Works Package stage.

Decanting residents for remediation works should be a last resort when no other option is available and not a choice. The decant must be planned thoroughly to mitigate the impact to residents. This can be done by:

partially phasing remediation works

decanting only essential units

This helps to lessen the time residents must live elsewhere and ensures value for money is achieved.

You will be asked to provide a sufficiently detailed decant strategy.

You should consider and evidence:

why any form of decant is needed — noting that CSS only funds this if it is essential to undertaking the eligible works

the options you have considered for the phasing and level of decant, and why you have arrived at this decision

You should detail the options you have considered for alternative accommodation, with serviced accommodation only proposed when all other options are not viable. For example:

use of vacant units in the block for partial or phased decants

engagement with residents and leaseholders to determine alternative arrangements such as staying with family and friends at a reduced cost

ensuring that alternative temporary accommodation reflects the basics of the existing accommodation (the same number of bedrooms, for example)

You must also consider and evidence the number of owner-occupied versus privately rented units.

For privately rented units, assess how many individual landlords this relates to and whether the Responsible Entity or any linked parties own any of these units.

CSS will not fund any loss of rental income arising from remediation works for landlords. It is the responsibility of all parties to manage tenancies effectively to mitigate their own loss.

We expect to see strong leaseholder and resident engagement delivered throughout.

Compiling your works package

Once the grant funding agreement is signed and you have started the monthly progress reports, you will be able to start compiling your works package.

Submit your works package at the same time as you make your submission to Building Control (if your works require it).

The first time you open the works package in the Building Remediation Hub it will be populated with information from the matching section in your most recent progress report. You should only open the section when you are ready to complete it. Updates in future progress reports will not update the works package in turn.

Including information already provided in your progress report, to complete the works package you will need to provide:

full details of your appointed project team including their contact information

confirmation of your grant certifying officer (read ‘The grant certifying officer and duty of care deed’)

planning permission progress

a Fire Risk Assessment and details of an internal defects if not already submitted at initial application stage

proposed works to cladding

a full proposed cost schedule (read ‘Cost schedule’)

details of any third-party financial contributions to the project

significant dates for project including start on site, date of cladding removal, as appropriate and completion date

You will need to appoint a professional team, scope the project and develop a works specification. The pre-tender support payment is designed to help with this and you should have the correct project team in place to begin this stage.

When you appoint your team, your lead designer will have the main responsibility for designing and specifying the works. Who fulfils this role can vary depending on the type of construction contract proposed. If your professional team is carrying out all the design and specification of the works, it’s likely that the lead designer will be a member of the team such as an architect or a façade engineer. If you are advised to use a ‘Design and Build’ type contract, the lead contractor may also carry out much of the design and will be the lead designer.

You must not appoint any party who was involved with the original works which are now being addressed by the CSS without prior specific agreement from Homes England. Consent will only be given by exception where we’re satisfied that appointing someone associated with the original installation is appropriate.

The grant certifying officer and duty of care deed

You will need to nominate either your quantity surveyor or project manager to act as the grant certifying officer[footnote 7] for your project. The grant certifying officer and their ‘consultant’ firm must be independent of the Responsible Entity and the contractor. The grant certifying officer will sign off individual grant claims and must:

be qualified in their field

be a member of a professional body

hold professional indemnity insurance

be knowledgeable and have significant experience relevant to the specific technical aspects

The firm that your grant certifying officer works for will need to enter into a duty of care deed with the Responsible Entity and Homes England. The duty of care deed is a legal document. It ensures that the individual and the firm[footnote 8] who sign off monthly grant claims have a duty of care to Homes England in undertaking the work as well as their responsibility to their client.

A template duty of care deed is made available so that the grant certifying officer firm can see the terms. This is for information only. We will send the actual document to be signed when appropriate.

If the grant certifying officer and, or, the firm they work for changes during the course of your project, let us know as soon as possible by emailing support@claddingsafetyscheme.co.uk. Quote the application reference number and building name in your email.

If the firm has changed, we will send a new duty of care deed to be signed by both the firm and the Responsible Entity and returned to us for signing and completion. You will not be able to draw down further funds until the new documents are signed and returned, and completed by Homes England, and all the relevant conditions have been met.

Changes to the grant certifying officer where the firm does not change do not need a new duty of care deed.

Cost schedule

You can only submit your cost schedule and works package once you have tendered and selected a preferred contractor to carry out the works. At that point, you’ll be able to provide the cost breakdown and answer the full works and costs related questions.

In addition to the cost information we will also ask you to:

confirm if you obtained competitive bids for the work and explain why, if not

identify the subcontractors that will be working on the project

confirm the cladding and insulation (type and manufacturer) that will be replacing the unsafe cladding being removed from your building

We will ask for a high-level breakdown of costs across the following areas:

cost of removing unsafe cladding (if applicable)

cost of installation of new cladding (if applicable)

preliminaries, access costs, main contractor’s overheads and profit

other costs (including FRAEW cost and irrecoverable VAT, reasonable costs of managing and administering the funding, and liaising with leaseholders and residents)

Compiling this information may require feedback from a number of people so we have provided a Microsoft Excel template within the system for you to download and collate the information prior to inputting it.

We expect costs, including fees to be reasonable and comparative within the market, and this will be checked as part of the review of your works package.

The costs you submit via the works package need to be for the whole project, including any expenditure incurred in the pre-tender stage. This enables us to consider the costs at project level prior to making a grant funding award. Later in the process you will be asked to account for the pre-tender support payment already made.

The cost schedule must show 100% of the costs. Where applicable, Homes England will apportion the costs for eligible units as part of the grant funding calculation. Do not submit pre-apportioned amounts as this may result in an incorrect grant award.

Should you have received any third-party contribution, be it an offer or actual payment, do not include these in the cost schedule. As above, the cost schedule must show 100% of the costs. You can add the details of the contribution separately as part of the works package and the system will include these in the calculation of grant funding.

You may be planning to undertake other works which you will fund yourself, alongside the works eligible for CSS funding. When we ask for a breakdown of costs, we also ask for high-level detail on the costs of any other ineligible works you are undertaking as part of the same works contract. This allows us to check that your monthly claims relate only to eligible costs while understanding the wider project and associated timelines.

If, once you have submitted your works package, you need to make any changes please contact us so that we can discuss those changes and update the project as needed.

VAT

You should only claim for any VAT you cannot recover - we call this irrecoverable VAT.

Snagging (the correction of faults) is often carried out after the building has been ‘completed’. Provided the replacement cladding or other works forms part of the original construction, and the person requesting the cladding or other works had an interest in the building during the construction works, then the replacement cladding may qualify for the zero rate as snagging. This work may form part of a building contract with zero-rated VAT.

Further information on the conditions of snagging can be found in the Construction VAT Manual VCONST02600 and paragraph 3.3.3 of VAT Notice 708.

For further information on VAT on remedial works, please refer to HMRC’s guidance for buildings and construction (VAT Notice 708) and HMRC internal manual: VAT construction .

Works package review

Once you have submitted your works package, we will review it and carry out additional checks including but not limited to reviewing the following:

the appointments of a professional team with appropriate qualifications, skills and experience and professional indemnity insurance

whether your costs for eligible works are reasonable and have been obtained via a competitive process

when you will start on site or execute the works contract. For the avoidance of doubt, this means when all parties formally agree and sign the final agreed version of the works contract

whether you have, or when you will have all statutory approvals

your forecast start on site and practical completion dates

leaseholder and resident engagement

We will contact you to clarify any questions or concerns we have and will work with you to address these. Upon the conclusion of our review, we will confirm the decision and next steps via email and the system. You can use this communication as proof of funding in principle to help you execute a works contract.

If your works package and costs are approved, you will receive the formal works package deed to sign. This in effect updates the grant funding agreement signed prior to pre-tender support to reflect the agreed grant payment total for the eligible works. Once executed by Homes England, this will be shared with you.

Project delivery

After you’ve been awarded funding and signed the works package deed, we’ll ask you to enter into a works contract with the main contractor.

Arrangements where third parties who are not the applicant, enter into a works contract on the applicant’s behalf will only be accepted in exceptional circumstances (for example, where two entities are responsible for works on different parts of the building). In such cases, we may ask for additional documentation showing how the funding we’ve provided is distributed between multiple entities, and their associated responsibilities.

One party cannot provide full consultancy services and act as, or appoint, the lead contractor. We’ve laid out below works contract requirements and other information you’ll need throughout your project.

Works contract requirements

The works contract should include the following:

A principal designer, for the purposes of Construction Design and Management Regulations 2015 (CDM Regs), must be named in the works contract and must meet the level of competence outlined in the regulations.

A contract administrator (CA), employer’s agent (EA) or architect must be named in the works contract. They must be responsible for administering the contract for the duration for the works. The CA, EA or architect must be a member of a chartered professional body (i.e. RICS, RIBA, CIOB etc) and appropriately experienced for the scale of the proposed works.

The main contractor named in the works contract must be appointed as the principal contractor under the Construction Design and Management Regulations 2015 (CDM Regs). The principal contractor must meet the level of competence described in the regulations and, if requested, evidence must be produced to verify this.

A quantity surveyor or cost consultant must be named in the contract and be responsible for contract valuations and cost monitoring. The quantity surveyor or cost consultant must be a member of a relevant chartered professional body (i.e. RICS).

A defects rectification period of a minimum of 12 months must be included in the contract and a minimum of 2.5% of the overall works contract value must be held as retention for this period. In addition, the works contract must include a provision for a minimum of 5% of the overall works contract value to be held as retention from commencement until practical completion of the works.

Adequate professional indemnity insurance must be stipulated in the works contract if the contractor is responsible for any design work. Its protection must cover the nature of the works and must not exclude cladding.

The contract must include an arbitration and/or adjudication procedure for dispute resolution.

The works contract must be executed as a deed, and this forms the works package deed. Evidence will need to be available on request that the contract has been executed as a deed to provide the maximum latent defects liability period.

Planning and building control

As part of any application, you should contact local authorities[footnote 9] and building control to facilitate the timely completion of design and development work to achieve an early start on site.

There will be a lead-in time to apply for and obtain planning permission. Your professional team will be able to advise you if planning permission is needed for your proposed works. Planning permission is distinct from building regulations approval which will always be required.

Building regulations

Building work carried out on a building must meet building regulations (The Building Regulations 2010), including minimum standards for fire safety and energy efficiency. (Please note these may be amended from time to time and following the introduction of secondary legislation pursuant to Part 3 of the Building Safety Act 2022.)

To ensure energy efficiency standards, building works to the external envelope of a building should adequately account for any changes in thermal bridges which may occur because of the work. They must also maintain or enhance the thermal performance of the external envelope of a building, where technically and economically feasible.

You may also wish to consider if there is an opportunity to use the project as a low-cost way to implement further energy efficiency measures that go beyond the current minimum requirements of the building regulations. Implementing other low-cost energy efficiency measures at the same time as works relating to the life safety fire risks associated with cladding may save you further cost and resource in the future. This is not mandatory and will not be considered as a condition of receiving funding. Any additional costs for these works, above those recommended in the FRAEW, should not form part of your application for CSS funding.

Schedule of works

Initial pre-tender support may have been paid to you upfront. The remaining grant award to enable you to complete the works will be paid monthly in arrears based on submission of your claims containing evidence of expenditure. Your chosen contractor must be made aware of the monthly payments schedule (in arrears) during the procurement process. They must also agree with the reporting schedule to enable applicants to meet the terms of the grant funding agreement.

Following the approval of the works package, the signing of the works package deed with Homes England and entering into the works contract, you will then need to create your schedule of works.

At this stage we will be asking for further information about your project delivery, which includes:

providing the signed works contract

uploading evidence of Building Control approval for works (Local authority or approved inspector for under 18 metres, or the Building Safety Regulator Gateway 2 approval if your building is over 18 metres or 7 storeys or more)

confirmation of the start and end months for the forecasted payment claim schedule

a monthly cashflow for eligible costs that were approved as part of the works package (‘costs profile’)

It is expected that the contractor and project team should be able to provide the information to complete the forecasted costs schedule.

The start month given for the first payment request must be at least one month in the future. This is because CSS payment links open at the start of each month, so you must submit your schedule of works in advance of month end to ensure sufficient time for this to be reviewed and approved ahead of the system generating your first scheduled payment link. You cannot submit a schedule of works with a start date in the current month.

The information provided in the schedule will give us a picture of when you hope to complete your project and a monthly profile of your project’s grant claims and payments. Grant is paid monthly in arrears and we require confirmation from the grant certifying officer at each monthly claim that the works have been undertaken and the incurred costs are eligible for funding.

The cost profile submitted at schedule of works is your initial forecast, which we will rely upon. We understand that things can change over the course of a project and each month you will have the opportunity to amend the forecast in line with changes.

Once you have submitted your schedule of works, we will review this to ensure that the overall cost profile reflects the grant funding award. As a condition of funding, 5% of the total grant award is retained. At this point we will adjust your final monthly claim to reflect the 5% retention. The final payment of 5% will be paid on full completion of the project and subject to you providing evidence of achievement in line with the contractual requirements as set out in the closing report.

If we have any queries relating to your schedule of works submission, we will contact you before progressing a decision. Once approved, you will receive an email notification and will be able to see your approved schedule, including the 5% retention within the system.

Self-certification

You must self-certify several critical aspects concerning your project and application.

Self-certification is the process whereby the applicant provides assurance (with recourse to third parties) that they and their supply chain have complied with all their contractual obligations to Homes England in completing the works to cladding. For example, you must certify that all parties contracted to you to deliver the works related to life safety fire risks associated with cladding have complied with the requirements of their respective contracts.

As part of the grant funding agreement, you must confirm that your self-certification statements are correct and accurate. If you are using a representative to act on your behalf, you must satisfy yourself that the project documentation and professional appointments have been correctly established in line with the requirements set by the CSS.

You’ll need to put processes in place that provide evidence to enable you to self-certify. These processes should help you confirm that the works are being completed correctly and in line with the fund requirements.

Your contractor must ensure that all non-conformances or defects are reported and demonstrate to your project manager that they have been satisfactorily resolved. We require you to make sure your contractor implements and confirms a system for the provision of evidence at all points throughout the works as part of their management and project administration arrangements. Once the works are complete, a certificate should be signed between you and the contractor to confirm that the works have been completed to the required standard outlined in the fund requirements.

Monthly payment requests

The Cladding Safety Scheme pays funding monthly in arrears once a start on site is achieved. Your chosen contractor must be made aware of the monthly payments schedule (in arrears) during the procurement process. They must also agree with the reporting schedule to enable applicants to meet the terms of the grant funding agreement.

You must complete and submit a monthly payment request in the system under the terms of your funding agreement. You must submit the payment request within the first 5 working days of each month to ensure you are paid promptly and within the calendar month.

If a payment request is not submitted on time an escalation meeting is held to discuss the impact of missing the funding payment. The responsible entity (if not you) is invited to attend.

You must make a £0 claim using the system if you have not made a financial drawdown in a particular month. You will be asked to provide an explanation about why the forecast drawdown cannot be met.

Any future payments must be reforecast if your payment claim is different from the forecast amount.

All payments must be forecast accurately so that we can work with HM Treasury to manage the fund effectively.

Your bank account must be active when you submit a payment request. Late requests for changes to bank account details may result in a delay processing your payment. If you need to change the bank details for your application, you must let us know immediately and prior to the change if possible.

In addition to the request for funding, each month you need to provide some information about your project. This must include:

confirmation of the grant funding you wish to claim

a signed cost report from your grant certifying officer, with supporting evidence

your latest project milestone dates

whether your project costs have changed

if there have been any changes to your project team

the date and evidence of your latest leaseholder and resident communication

Payment will be contingent on a cost report signed off by your grant certifying officer with supporting evidence for eligible expenditure to date.

You can download a template cost report from the Building Remediation Hub to help provide information to us in a standard format.

If you use your own cost report format, it must:

be signed, dated and submitted by the grant certifying officer

be on their firm’s headed paper

include the building name

include the Cladding Safety Scheme application reference number

The cost report should cover invoices received. The breakdown of claim should include all 5 entries (all exclusive of VAT), including nil, if applicable, for amounts included in this claim:

Works

Professional fees in relation to works

Managing agent’s and other fees

Other costs

Irrecoverable VAT

The sum of these entries should amount to the total claim.

Invoices should be submitted for all qualifying costs as part of the relevant monthly payment claim. These should be supplied to us as 1 combined file saved in PDF format for ease of reconciliation.

If the cost report and invoices do not fully align to the payment request, the claim will not be approved. We will contact you to work through any discrepancies, but this may result in a rejected claim, partial payment or delayed payment approval.

For funding to be paid, you must ensure that payments by you to your advisers and works contractor are made only in respect of work completed. Applicants are responsible for ensuring that payments are made on time to the consultants and contractors to prevent avoidable delays. Costs associated with these delays are not eligible for funding. We will not accept arrangements which are not industry standard, under which consultants or the contractor are paid in advance of the satisfactory completion of works.

First payment request

Your first monthly payment claim for a project should cover the information set out in Monthly payment requests.

Additional evidence is required if your application received a pre-tender support (PTS) payment.

The cost report for your first monthly payment claim must include:

the full pre-tender amount received

all eligible project costs incurred to date

all relevant invoices for qualifying expenditure

any invoices associated with pre-tender support spend

Example

You have received £200,000 in pre-tender support and incurred further costs of £50,000.

Your first monthly payment claim is for £50,000.

The cost report is for £250,000.

If the cost report for your first monthly payment claim does not cover the full amount of pre-tender support paid, your first monthly claim will not be approved.

You can resubmit your first monthly claim when your pre-tender support payment has been exhausted, and additional expenditure has been incurred.

Variations

You must manage the total eligible costs of your project within the grant funding amount you are awarded. We appreciate that circumstances change, and costs may increase due to unforeseen overruns or alterations to the scope of the contract. If that happens, you’ll need to apply via the system for a variation to the grant sum that was approved under your grant funding agreement. Homes England commit to considering such requests as swiftly as possible and will confirm in writing if your request is approved.

We appreciate that there may be certain circumstances where the project costs can decrease as well as increase. Where that is the case, please contact us directly to discuss the changes.

Variations in grant sums may be permitted for (but not limited to) the following reasons:

to comply with statutory requirements (e.g. building, town planning or CDM regulations, etc.)

Homes England reserves the right to consider each application to vary the grant on its own circumstances and merits and is under no obligation to approve these.

Construction contracts differ in the placement of liability in relation to variations. The cost variation will only be permitted if the liability for the variation is neither yours nor the contractors.

Consultants, such as designers, have responsibilities under their professional appointments. If the additional project costs have arisen through the inadequate performance of a consultant’s duties under their appointment, the sum may be recoverable from the consultant or from their professional indemnity insurance (PII). In these circumstances, we’ll expect you to recover the costs from the relevant consultant, or their insurer, and additional grant sums will not be made available.

The party responsible for valuing variations would usually be named in an industry-standard construction contract. In addition to the named party’s contractual responsibilities, it is advisable that the same entity be responsible for submission of applications for variations in grant sums on your behalf as nominated representative.

The party responsible for submission of the application will need to provide details of the cost variations and how they have been calculated. Costs could be related to:

professional fees

construction costs

site set-up and preliminaries

a combination of the above

If cost variations are being sought, you must retain information to prove that the cost variations relate only to the works permitted for grant funding and/or works needed to facilitate them.

We’ll rely on your grant certifying officer to rigorously check all costs and they’ll have to enter into a duty of care agreement with Homes England.

Practical completion — scheme exit

At the point of practical completion for your project, and ahead of your final payment being made, you must submit a closing report using the Building Remediation Hub.

Your report must provide Homes England with evidence covering all of the following points.

Total project spend

This must be signed off by your grant certifying officer with all supporting evidence provided.

Homes England may use independent cost consultants to fully review project spend to provide assurance it is in line with the grant award and covers eligible works only. The cumulative funding figure will be published on the subsidy transparency database.

Building control sign off

This must be signed off by the appropriate regulatory body.

Homes England will not make final payments until the relevant certification has been provided.

It is the responsibility of the applicant to work with their contractors to ensure that any part of the works requiring action is satisfactorily addressed and fully signed off.

Practical completion certification

Evidence of practical completion certification must be provided.

An updated Fire Risk Assessment (FRA)

The Fire Risk Assessment must be updated and show eligible works identified in the Fire Risk Appraisal of External Wall (FRAEW) have been completed, including who carried these out and when.

The evacuation strategy must be updated after any works identified in the FRAEW have been carried out.

Sign off from Building Control is needed and must show works have reduced the risk-to-life rating to a tolerable level.

Blocks of flats also require a Fire Risk Assessment to be in place. Homes England uses the established process and documentation required for management of each building. The Responsible Entity must determine the type of FRA that is appropriate as part of their ongoing management of the building.

Informing residents and leaseholders about the completion of the remediation project

You must include evidence of communicating to residents and leaseholders about completion of the remediation project.

You must include a link to the Cladding Safety Scheme — Leaseholder and residents’ survey (Hosted on Microsoft Forms) as part of this communication.

Your position in relation to clause 5.4 of the Grant Funding Arrangement

As part of your report you must set out your position in relation to clause 5.4 of the Grant Funding Arrangement in as much detail as you can.

You must include all entities including:

the developer

any supply chain party

any warranty provider

Public funds have been provided to enable early remediation and ensuring these can be recovered is part of your contractual obligation. Including the most recent supporting evidence or correspondence will allow us to do this.

Building insurance

You’ll be asked to provide buildings insurance documentation upon completion of your remediation works. This will include:

the total sum insured

the insurance premium

the name of the insurance provider

Sharing this information helps Homes England and Ministry for Housing, Communities and Local Government report on post-remediation benefits and changes to premiums.

Open book access

The CSS processes follow the government’s approach to open-book contract management. These help Homes England maintain a clear line of sight between the cost requirements for eligible works compared to the Homes England funds granted. A low cost, minimal open-book approach is applied, which gives us assurance that value for money is being achieved, as required by Managing Public Money for Government grant schemes.

Therefore, you’ll need to submit any relevant supporting documents requested by Homes England. You’ll need to keep on record any other documents that you’ve confirmed you have obtained so they are available on request. The grant funding agreement stipulates that Homes England and appointed third parties are given access to required information and documentation.

During works, Homes England has the right to request from you cost details and any supporting documentation. The CSS will retain specialist support (e.g., legal, commercial, technical advisors) who will have the same open book access rights.

After completion, a sample of projects may be randomly selected or targeted for potential government audit activities (e.g. National Audit Office value-for-money studies). You’ll be responsible for providing your own resources for these audits. We recommend that you allow for this potential scope in your consultants’ appointments. Funding such activity is not an eligible cost.
